correctness.rationale: Define D(r)=r xor next r; Q(r)=¬F D(r), P(r)=r xor Q(r). On W=N0×N0 with spatial order along i at fixed j and temporal successor (i,j+1), let p=(i even), q=(j>=i), r=p xor q. Along each temporal orbit r changes exactly once at j=i for i>=1, never for i=0, so Q=q and P=p. Substituting these two observations into the four Vooijs–Fernández-Duque conditions yields satisfiability at (0,0). The obstruction proof requires only arbitrary formula observations a,b: in any finite generated spatial upset, the alternating spatial successor relation produces mutually accessible points with opposite a. Formula 1 keeps a and makes b persistent along time; formulas 3/4 produce conflicting eventual b witnesses, and comparing their witness times contradicts persistence and monotonicity. Hence no finite generated upset. All variable-free formulae are spatially and temporally constant (for nonempty reflexive frames) and thus satisfiable on a singleton iff satisfiable anywhere; one genuine atom is sharp. The source proof and original two-variable Lemma 3.1 were inspected side by side, including the page image.
